title: Add armed-mode recovery protection
description:
## Problem Statement

Armed enforcement can currently lock macOS from a forbidden-proximity violation, but the recovery story is not safe enough for real-beacon validation. A CLI/TUI panic command is not a true fail-safe because it cannot help while the Mac is locked or when an overlay makes interaction confusing. The user needs Faraday to preserve weak-moment resistance without trapping them in unintended lock or overlay loops when the phone and computer must be close together.

## Solution

Add daemon-owned armed-mode recovery protection before continuing real-beacon armed validation. Armed enforcement gets a default timebox, post-unlock cooldown, repeat-lock countdown, and repeated-lock circuit breaker. The overlay becomes prominent but non-modal, never stealing keyboard or mouse interaction. Missing and uncertain proximity remain non-locking classifications. The TUI exposes a single guided setup flow plus dashboard state for armed time remaining, cooldowns, countdowns, circuit-breaker state, and recovery-protection pause reasons.

## User Stories

1. As a distracted Mac user, I want armed enforcement to be timeboxed during MVP validation, so that one experiment cannot leave native lock authority active longer than intended.
2. As a distracted Mac user, I want first real-beacon armed validation capped to about 5 minutes, so that testing real lock behavior feels safe.
3. As a distracted Mac user, I want armed timebox expiry to switch Faraday to dry-run, so that expired validation cannot lock my Mac.
4. As a distracted Mac user, I want armed timebox expiry to hide active violation countdown UI, so that the UI matches the new non-locking state.
5. As a distracted Mac user, I want timebox expiry logged, so that I can understand why enforcement mode changed.
6. As a distracted Mac user, I want a cooldown after unlocking from a Faraday lock, so that I regain immediate access to the computer.
7. As a distracted Mac user, I want post-unlock cooldown to last about 2 minutes, so that I can handle legitimate phone-and-computer-close moments.
8. As a distracted Mac user, I want cooldown to warn without locking, so that Faraday remains honest without trapping me.
9. As a distracted Mac user, I want acceptable proximity during cooldown to return the session to normal active enforcement, so that moving the phone away resolves the violation cleanly.
10. As a distracted Mac user, I want missing proximity during cooldown to degrade beacon trust without locking, so that BLE dropouts do not punish me.
11. As a distracted Mac user, I want uncertain proximity during cooldown to warn without locking, so that ambiguous RSSI never causes a native lock.
12. As a distracted Mac user, I want repeat locks to use a countdown, so that Faraday never instantly relocks after cooldown.
13. As a distracted Mac user, I want repeat countdowns to be shorter than the first violation countdown, so that repeated violations still create pressure without being silent.
14. As a distracted Mac user, I want repeat countdowns to cancel when acceptable proximity is sustained, so that moving the phone away always resolves the problem.
15. As a distracted Mac user, I want repeated lock requests to trip a circuit breaker, so that unstable calibration or placement cannot create a hostile lock loop.
16. As a distracted Mac user, I want the MVP circuit breaker threshold to be 2 lock requests within 10 minutes, so that the second lock proves instability and the third lock never happens automatically.
17. As a distracted Mac user, I want the circuit breaker to switch enforcement to dry-run, so that native lock authority is disabled after repeated lock requests.
18. As a distracted Mac user, I want the circuit breaker to hide active countdown UI, so that I can use the Mac normally after protection trips.
19. As a distracted Mac user, I want the circuit breaker to require explicit re-arm, so that Faraday cannot silently resume native lock authority.
20. As a distracted Mac user, I want the overlay to be prominent but non-modal, so that I notice violations without losing access to the desktop.
21. As a distracted Mac user, I want the overlay to never steal keyboard or mouse interaction, so that overlay bugs do not block recovery.
22. As a distracted Mac user, I want overlay copy to explain cooldown, countdown, and circuit-breaker state, so that I know what Faraday is doing.
23. As a distracted Mac user, I want the TUI dashboard to show armed time remaining, so that I know how long native lock authority remains active.
24. As a distracted Mac user, I want the TUI dashboard to show cooldown remaining, so that I know when repeat enforcement may resume.
25. As a distracted Mac user, I want the TUI dashboard to show circuit-breaker state, so that I know why armed enforcement is disabled.
26. As a distracted Mac user, I want `panic` language replaced or demoted, so that Faraday does not imply a CLI command is sufficient when the Mac is locked.
27. As a distracted Mac user, I want setup to be a single guided flow, so that installation, beacon selection, calibration, dry-run rehearsal, and armed validation are less tedious.
28. As a distracted Mac user, I want real-beacon armed validation paused until recovery protection exists, so that validation does not risk lock loops.
29. As a contributor, I want recovery protection owned by the daemon, so that closing the TUI does not change enforcement semantics.
30. As a contributor, I want recovery-protection logic tested with mock enforcement, so that automated tests never lock macOS.
31. As a future GUI developer, I want recovery-protection state exposed through the daemon API, so that a later menu-bar or native app can reuse the same safety model.

## Implementation Decisions

- Build a deep daemon-core recovery-protection module that owns armed timebox, post-unlock cooldown, repeat countdown, circuit breaker, and pause reasons behind a small state-transition API.
- Keep lock decisions daemon-owned. The TUI and any future GUI remain control/display surfaces only.
- Add recovery-protection state to persisted status and JSON-RPC status: armed expiry, cooldown expiry or remaining seconds, repeat countdown state, circuit-breaker state, lock request window, and pause reason.
- Add recovery-protection event kinds for armed timebox expiry, cooldown start/end, repeat countdown start/cancel/expire, circuit breaker trip, and explicit re-arm.
- Armed mode is timeboxed by default during MVP validation. First real-beacon armed validation has a 5 minute cap.
- Armed timebox expiry switches enforcement to dry-run, hides active countdown overlay, records an event, and requires explicit arming for any later native lock authority.
- Post-unlock recheck no longer immediately requests another lock. It enters a 2 minute cooldown when the prior lock was Faraday-caused.
- During post-unlock cooldown, forbidden proximity may warn but cannot lock. Acceptable proximity returns to active enforcement. Missing proximity degrades beacon trust. Uncertain proximity remains non-locking.
- After cooldown, if forbidden proximity is still sustained, Faraday starts a repeat countdown of about 10-15 seconds before requesting another lock.
- Repeated lock circuit breaker threshold is 2 lock requests within 10 minutes.
- Circuit breaker action is dry-run enforcement, hidden countdown overlay, visible paused-by-recovery-protection session state, explicit re-arm required.
- Do not implement a safe-mode sentinel file for MVP.
- Preserve missing/uncertain never-lock rules in all recovery-protection branches.
- Convert the overlay contract from a generic violation show/hide command toward stateful non-modal display updates that can render countdown, cooldown, armed time remaining, and circuit-breaker copy.
- The overlay must remain non-modal: prominent, always-on-top where feasible, visible across displays where feasible, but not stealing keyboard or mouse interaction.
- Update the TUI dashboard and guided setup flow to present recovery-protection state clearly.
- Guided setup flow order: health check, daemon/LaunchAgent state, beacon scan/select or manual entry, calibration, confidence display, dry-run rehearsal, explicit capped armed validation, dashboard/log handoff.
- Rename or demote user-facing `panic` framing. If a command remains, describe it as an unlocked recovery command, not a locked-screen fail-safe.
- Defer native GUI/menu-bar implementation. Design is tracked separately and must reuse the daemon API.

## Testing Decisions

- Test external behavior and state transitions, not implementation details.
- Automated tests must use mock enforcement adapters and must never call native macOS lock.
- Add daemon-core state-machine tests for armed timebox expiry, dry-run transition, overlay hide/update, and recovery-protection event emission.
- Add post-unlock cooldown tests for forbidden, acceptable, missing, and uncertain classifications.
- Add repeat countdown tests verifying no instant relock and cancellation on acceptable proximity.
- Add circuit-breaker tests verifying 2 lock requests within 10 minutes trips dry-run and explicit re-arm is required.
- Add no-lock classification regression tests proving missing and uncertain cannot trigger native lock in normal, cooldown, repeat-countdown, and circuit-breaker states.
- Add JSON-RPC/status tests proving recovery-protection fields are exposed and stable for TUI/future GUI clients.
- Add overlay adapter/orchestration tests proving countdown/cooldown/circuit-breaker state is shown or hidden at the right external states without rendering real UI.
- Add TUI render-state tests where practical for guided setup and recovery-protection dashboard mapping; avoid brittle terminal-art snapshots.
- Manual real-beacon validation resumes only after tests pass and the armed path is capped with recovery protection.

## Out of Scope

- Safe-mode sentinel file behavior.
- Adversarial tamper resistance against a determined local admin.
- Root LaunchDaemon serious mode.
- Native GUI or menu-bar implementation before Working MVP validation.
- Cloud accounts, telemetry, or phone-side app work.
- Locking from missing or uncertain proximity.
- Treating a CLI/TUI panic command as a locked-screen fail-safe.

## Further Notes

This PRD refines `docs/PRD.md` rather than replacing the Working MVP PRD. `faraday-alk.16` real-beacon validation now depends on this work because armed validation should not continue until recovery protection exists. A separate backlog issue tracks future native GUI/menu-bar design after the Working MVP proves the daemon API and core flows.

title: Run real-beacon Working MVP validation
description:
## Parent

faraday-alk

## What to build

Run real-beacon Working MVP validation end-to-end with the physical beacon and real Mac session: setup, calibration, strict session, violation overlay, armed lock, unlock repeat countdown, missing degradation, logs, and follow-up issue capture.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Real beacon can be selected and calibrated.
- [ ] Strict session activates only after acceptable proximity.
- [ ] Forbidden proximity shows overlay and locks in armed mode after countdown.
- [ ] Unlock while still forbidden triggers repeat countdown.
- [ ] Missing beacon degrades trust and does not lock from missing alone.
- [ ] Logs provide evidence for pass/fail and any follow-up issues are filed.

## Blocked by

- Add dry-run and armed lock enforcement
- Add unlock notification recheck flow
- Validate real iBeacon scanner hardware path
- Add TUI calibration wizard
- Add missing-beacon degraded recovery
- Smoke-test user LaunchAgent in macOS
acceptance_criteria: See acceptance criteria in issue body.
notes: Real-beacon validation paused before armed lock testing. User confirmed armed-mode recovery protection must exist first: armed timebox, post-unlock cooldown, repeated-lock circuit breaker, non-modal overlay, no safe-mode sentinel, missing/uncertain never lock. faraday-alk.16 now depends on faraday-alk.17.

title: Add missing-beacon degraded recovery
description:
## Parent

faraday-alk

## What to build

Add the missing-beacon degraded recovery flow. Missing during active strict session invalidates/degrades enforcement, warns clearly, never locks from missing alone, and requires forbidden revalidation followed by acceptable proximity to resume.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Missing timeout during active session enters degraded beacon-trust state.
- [ ] Degraded state shows overlay/TUI warning and records events.
- [ ] Missing alone never requests native lock.
- [ ] Recovery requires forbidden revalidation then acceptable proximity before active enforcement resumes.

## Blocked by

- Add calibrated proximity classifier
- Add daemon core with JSON persistence
- Add native overlay helper and orchestration
acceptance_criteria: See acceptance criteria in issue body.

title: Add calibrated proximity classifier
description:

- [ ] Confidence reports good, weak, or unusable based on separation and overlap.
- [ ] Weak or unusable confidence blocks armed enforcement eligibility.
- [ ] Synthetic RSSI tests cover forbidden, acceptable, uncertain, missing, noisy boundary, and recovery scenarios.

title: Add local persistence and event log
description:
## What to build
Persist local state and event records needed to inspect whether Faraday works. Store settings, calibration data if present, session lifecycle events, warnings, violations, lock events, missing-beacon events, and emergency events. Expose current status for a future local dashboard.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Settings for configured beacon and classifier thresholds save and load locally.
- [ ] Session, violation, missing-beacon, lock, and emergency events record timestamps.
- [ ] Current daemon/session status can be read through a local boundary.
- [ ] Persistence tests verify emitted records for major transitions.
- [ ] No cloud account, sync, subscription, or remote analytics dependency is introduced.

## Blocked by
faraday-4a0, faraday-heq, faraday-dk5

title: Integrate beacon allowlist scanner
description:
## What to build
Connect CoreBluetooth scanning to the classifier input shape. The scanner should discover advertisements for a configured iBeacon and emit timestamped RSSI observations only when UUID plus major/minor match the allowlist.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Config supports identifying the configured beacon by UUID plus major/minor.
- [ ] Scanner emits timestamped RSSI observations in the classifier input shape.
- [ ] Non-matching BLE advertisements are ignored.
- [ ] Scanner lifecycle can start and stop cleanly.
- [ ] Manual/integration notes describe validation with a real configurable iBeacon.

## Blocked by
faraday-dy6

title: Implement missing-beacon enforcement path
description:
## What to build
Implement missing-beacon behavior during and outside strict sessions. Missing outside strict session warns only. Missing after near or unknown during strict session is unsafe. Missing after far-confirmed enters grace, then unsafe if grace expires.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Missing outside strict session does not lock and emits warning/status only.
- [ ] Missing after near or unknown during strict session is unsafe.
- [ ] Missing after far-confirmed enters grace/warning instead of instant lock.
- [ ] Missing beyond configured grace emits unsafe enforcement behavior.
- [ ] Tests cover missing outside session, after far, after near, and grace expiry.

## Blocked by
faraday-heq

title: Implement strict session start flow
description:
## What to build
Implement strict session startup through the session state machine. Starting focus requires the configured beacon to be alive and near, then instructs the user to move the phone away, and activates only after sustained far confirmation.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Start Focus is refused when the beacon is missing.
- [ ] Start Focus is refused or held when the beacon is not confirmed near/alive.
- [ ] Near confirmation emits a move-phone-away instruction.
- [ ] Session becomes active only after sustained far confirmation.
- [ ] Tests cover missing-at-start, near-confirmed setup, transient far, and sustained far activation.

## Blocked by
faraday-dy6

title: Implement unsafe proximity lock path
description:
## What to build
Implement the active-session path where the beacon becomes near again. Sustained near should enter an unsafe countdown, emit a warning overlay command, cancel if far-confirmed returns, and emit a native-lock command if unsafe persists.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Active session enters warning/countdown after sustained near violation.
- [ ] Countdown emits an overlay-ready enforcement command.
- [ ] Countdown cancels when far-confirmed returns before expiry.
- [ ] Lock command emits when unsafe state persists through countdown.
- [ ] Post-unlock recheck relocks or re-enters enforcement when still unsafe.
- [ ] Tests verify lock decisions through a mock adapter only.

## Blocked by
faraday-4a0

title: Implement RSSI classification tracer
description:
## What to build
Build the first end-to-end tracer for RSSI classification. Synthetic timestamped observations for a configured beacon should produce near, far, uncertain, or missing classifications using smoothing, hysteresis, and sustained-time rules.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Synthetic RSSI observations feed the classifier without CoreBluetooth.
- [ ] Defaults classify sustained strong RSSI as near and sustained weak RSSI as far.
- [ ] Missing classification occurs after the configured timeout.
- [ ] Boundary noise does not rapidly flap between near and far.
- [ ] Tests cover sustained near, brief near spike, sustained far, missing timeout, and noisy boundary behavior.

## Blocked by
faraday-ned

title: Scaffold Swift macOS app core
description:
## What to build
Create the initial Swift macOS app/daemon scaffold with testable module boundaries for Faraday. Establish empty seams for scanner input, RSSI classification, strict session state, enforcement, calibration, persistence, and launchd integration.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Repo has a minimal Swift macOS project/package structure.
- [ ] At least one core module and one test target exist.
- [ ] Placeholder interfaces or types exist for each deep module boundary.
- [ ] Test target runs with a smoke test.
- [ ] No automated test can lock the developer Mac.

## Blocked by

title: Build end-to-end MVP validation harness
description:
## What to build
Create the real-world MVP validation harness for Faraday: manual beacon validation, setup checklist, session test script, five-workday usage review, and metric capture for phone-at-desk time, false lockouts, emergency use, and bypass attempts.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Checklist covers hardware setup for a configurable iBeacon attached to the phone/case.
- [ ] Manual script validates session start, far activation, near violation countdown/lock, missing-beacon grace/lock, and emergency mode.
- [ ] Five-workday review template captures two sessions per day, phone-at-desk duration, false lockouts, emergency use, and bypass attempts.
- [ ] Validation records whether PRD success metrics pass or fail.
- [ ] Findings can feed future Beads issues.

## Blocked by
faraday-eck, faraday-c9p, faraday-16z, faraday-wnv

title: Decide launchd weak-moment resistance posture
description:
## What to build
Make the human-reviewed launchd and weak-moment resistance decision. Decide whether MVP uses a user LaunchAgent, root-owned LaunchDaemon, or staged support for both, then capture the tradeoff as an ADR and install/remove docs.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Human-reviewed decision records user LaunchAgent vs root-owned LaunchDaemon vs staged support.
- [ ] docs/adr/ contains an ADR for launchd enforcement posture.
- [ ] Install, restart, and remove steps are documented.
- [ ] KeepAlive/restart behavior is included for MVP operation.
- [ ] Docs state weak-moment resistance limits clearly for local-admin users.
- [ ] Smoke/manual test instructions verify startup and restart behavior.

## Blocked by
faraday-heq, faraday-y1t

title: Validate first real beacon with scanner
description:
## What to build
Validate one real bring-your-own compatible iBeacon with the Faraday scanner and classifier. Use the result to update the compatibility list with concrete device status and setup notes.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] At least one real configurable iBeacon is tested with the scanner.
- [ ] UUID, major/minor, transmit power, advertising interval, and battery notes are recorded where available.
- [ ] Desk and target-room RSSI behavior is captured.
- [ ] docs/BEACONS.md lists the device as tested, likely-compatible, or unsupported.
- [ ] Any scanner or classifier gaps discovered during validation become Beads issues.

## Blocked by
faraday-7za and hardware in hand

title: Implement guided calibration path
description:
## What to build
Implement optional guided calibration for RSSI thresholds. The user measures beacon RSSI at desk, doorway/hall, and target room. Calibration derives near/far thresholds and confidence notes while preserving defaults when skipped.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Calibration collects labeled sample sets for desk, doorway/hall, and target room.
- [ ] Calibration output includes derived near/far thresholds and confidence notes.
- [ ] Defaults remain available when calibration is skipped or incomplete.
- [ ] Calibration data is stored separately from live RSSI observations.
- [ ] Tests cover representative desk, doorway, and target-room sample sets.

## Blocked by
faraday-dy6, faraday-y1t

title: Implement Emergency Co-work Mode
description:
## What to build
Implement Emergency Co-work Mode as a short, logged exception during a strict session. The user provides a reason, waits through a deliberate delay, receives 10 minutes of phone-and-Mac coexistence, can extend once, then must move the phone far again.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Emergency mode requires a user-provided reason.
- [ ] Emergency mode starts only after a configured 30-60 second delay.
- [ ] Emergency mode suppresses unsafe near-lock behavior for the configured duration.
- [ ] Exactly one extension is allowed and later extension attempts are refused.
- [ ] Emergency start, extension, refusal, and expiration events are logged.
- [ ] After expiration, strict session requires far-confirmed before normal continuation.

## Blocked by
faraday-heq, faraday-y1t

title: Draft beacon compatibility buying guide
description:
## What to build
Create the first useful beacon compatibility and buying guide for bring-your-own iBeacons before scanner implementation exists. Focus on what users should buy, which settings matter, and how future validation will be recorded.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] docs/BEACONS.md explains required beacon capabilities.
- [ ] Buying guidance distinguishes tested, likely-compatible, and unsupported devices.
- [ ] Recommended starting settings are documented without requiring Faraday-branded hardware.
- [ ] Validation checklist is ready for later real-device testing.

## Blocked by
None - can start immediately
close_reason: Repo planning centralized in docs and Beads; open-source foundation and initial beacon compatibility guide added.

title: Design native GUI/menu-bar control surface
description:
## What to design

Design a future native macOS GUI or menu-bar app for Faraday setup, beacon management, calibration, session status, and recovery controls.

## Scope

- Reuse the daemon JSON-RPC API.
- GUI has no enforcement authority and never directly locks macOS.
- Support install/check, beacon scan/select, calibration, dry-run rehearsal, armed validation, dashboard, and recovery-protection state.
- Preserve local-first behavior: no cloud, no accounts, no telemetry.
- Compare menu-bar-first, windowed setup wizard, and hybrid approaches.

## Out of scope

- Implementation before Working MVP validation.
- Any paid software feature split.
- Replacing daemon-owned session/enforcement logic.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] UX option chosen: menu-bar app, windowed app, or hybrid.
- [ ] Required daemon API additions identified.
- [ ] Setup/calibration/recovery flows mapped.
- [ ] ADR proposed if GUI becomes primary control surface.

title: Evaluate recommended beacon kit viability
description:
## What to build
After real-world validation, evaluate whether Faraday should move from compatibility-list-only to a recommended third-party beacon kit. Keep this as product strategy, not MVP software scope.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Decision uses validation harness findings and beacon compatibility evidence.
- [ ] Recommendation says stay compatibility-list-only, sell recommended kit, or defer.
- [ ] If kit is recommended, required support, warranty, fulfillment, and setup-material work is listed as follow-up.
- [ ] Decision preserves bring-your-own beacon as a first-class path.

## Blocked by
faraday-5zr
